question: Can one positive dye-cloud diffusion scale per colour layer, fitted only from development MTF frequencies, predict both held-frequency MTF and independently realized Poisson NPS shape across held densities better than no diffusion and wrong-layer scales?
claim_ceiling: generic synthetic joint dye-cloud MTF/NPS identifiability evidence; no measured stock, process, scanner, photographic preference or product claim

source_basis.title: On Dye Cloud Diffusion and the Image Quality of Colour Negative Photographic Materials
Estimating the Size and Profile of Diffuse Dye Clouds in Colour Negative Film
source_basis.role: independent cloud-profile consistency across photomicrography, MTF and NPS

source_basis.title: ITU-T H.Sup21 Film grain synthesis technology for video applications
source_basis.role: latest standards context for dye-cloud rather than display-RGB noise semantics

split.rule: Fit sigma from development MTF only. Confirmation MTF, all Poisson fields and NPS-derived sigma estimates remain unread until all three layer sigmas are frozen.

candidate.shared_constraint: The same frozen layer sigma generates the signal MTF and predicts normalized NPS shape; independent MTF and NPS radii are forbidden in the primary candidate.

controls.nps_only_oracle: diagnostic only; may quantify finite-sample identifiability but cannot replace the MTF-fitted primary scale
controls.label_permutation: wrong-layer radii must not tie the correctly bound layer identities

forbidden_actions: fit sigma to confirmation MTF or NPS
give MTF and NPS separate primary radii
change layer mapping, seeds, densities, frequencies, grid or gates after confirmation
add display RGB noise or infer a stock/process/scanner profile
open photographic rendering, preference review or product integration from this synthetic result

branch_rule.pass: Retain one shared-scale joint dye-cloud signature primitive and next test it only against independently measured MTF plus NPS from the same material/process group.
branch_rule.fail: Close this exact Gaussian shared-scale hypothesis without adding mixture components or fitting confirmation; continue a distinct physical mechanism.
